issues.t: ABS module can short and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: Often no warning. Some owners see the ABS light come on, smell burning, or notice smoke from the engine bay, even with the car parked and off.
issues.why: On 2006-2011 cars, water can get into the anti-lock brake module and short it. On 2012-2015 cars, brake fluid can leak inside the module and cause a short. Either can start an engine compartment fire. Hyundai recalled both generations.
issues.next: Park outside and away from buildings until the fix is done. Check your VIN for recall 18V-026 (2006-2011) or 23V-651 (2012-2015).

issues.t: Rear crossmember rusts and control arm can come loose (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the rear over bumps, the car pulling or wandering, uneven tire wear, or heavy rust on the rear subframe.
issues.why: Road salt can corrode the rear crossmember until a rear lower control arm mount lets go, which suddenly changes the wheel alignment. Hyundai recalled cars in salt-belt states.
issues.next: Have the rear crossmember inspected, especially if you live where roads are salted. Check your VIN for recall 13V-354.

issues.t: Front passenger airbag may not deploy (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light may come on, or there may be no sign at all.
issues.why: Repeated use of the front passenger seat belt can damage the wiring to its tension sensor, which can stop the passenger front airbag from deploying in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 09V-497. Have the airbag light checked promptly if it is on.

issues.t: Brake lights may not work (recall)
issues.sym: Brake lights stay off or stay on, cruise control will not cancel when braking, the stability control light comes on, or the shifter can leave Park without the brake pressed.
issues.why: The brake light switch can fail. Hyundai recalled it in several campaigns covering these years.
issues.next: Have someone check your brake lights. Check your VIN for recalls 09V-280, 09V-122 and 13V-113.

issues.t: Driver's power seat moves by itself (recall)
issues.sym: The driver's seat or seat back moves forward or back on its own while driving.
issues.why: A faulty power seat switch on cars built March-August 2007 can move the seat without input, which can affect your control of the car.
issues.next: If the seat moves on its own, stop safely. Check your VIN for recall 16V-630; the dealer replaces the switch for free.

issues.t: Valve cover gasket oil leak onto alternator
issues.sym: Burning oil smell, oil on top of the engine or dripping on the alternator, and later a battery light, dim lights or a dead charging system.
issues.why: The valve cover gaskets and spark plug tube seals harden and leak. Oil from the front cover can soak the alternator below it and make it fail. Repeat leaks are common.
issues.next: Have leaks fixed early, before oil ruins the alternator. Replace both gaskets and the plug tube seals together.

issues.t: Cold-start ticking or rattle from the engine
issues.sym: A ticking, rattling or knocking sound for a few seconds after a cold start, sometimes longer.
issues.why: Timing chain tensioners can let the chain slap on start-up, and Hyundai issued a bulletin to replace them. Some cases were traced to piston slap, and a few owners got a new engine block under warranty.
issues.next: Have a dealer listen on a true cold start and check for the tensioner bulletin. Keep oil changes on time with the correct grade.

issues.t: Throttle sensor fault causes stalling or limp mode
issues.sym: Check engine light, sluggish or no acceleration, the car stuck at low speed, rough running or stalling.
issues.why: The throttle position sensor in the electronic throttle body fails on these cars. Fixes usually include a new sensor or throttle body and an engine computer update.
issues.next: Have the codes read right away. Ask the dealer to check for the engine computer update with the sensor repair.

issues.t: Timing cover oil leak
issues.sym: Oil seeping from the front of the engine behind the drive belts, sometimes dripping onto the alternator.
issues.why: The front timing chain cover gasket and sealant can leak with age. The repair is labor heavy because the front of the engine must come apart.
issues.next: Watch the oil level. A small seep can be monitored, but fix it if oil is reaching the belts or alternator.

issues.t: Squealing or whining from drive belt idler pulley
issues.sym: A whistle, squeal or whine from the front of the engine, often worse on cold mornings.
issues.why: Bearings in the idler pulley and belt tensioner wear out and get noisy.
issues.next: Have the pulleys spun by hand to find the bad one. Replace the belt at the same time if it is cracked.

issues.t: Crankshaft pulley (harmonic balancer) failure
issues.sym: Squealing on start-up, a wobbling pulley at the front of the engine, or the belt slipping off.
issues.why: The rubber layer in the crankshaft pulley breaks down so the outer ring loosens.
issues.next: Have it replaced soon. A loose pulley can throw the belt, which stops the alternator and water pump.

issues.t: Dashboard cracks
issues.sym: Cracks open in the top of the dashboard, sometimes near the passenger airbag.
issues.why: The dashboard surface breaks down from heat and sun.
issues.next: Use a sunshade. A cracked dash near the airbag should be checked, and a full dash replacement is labor heavy.

issues.t: Clunking from front sway bar links
issues.sym: A knock or clunk from the front over bumps and rough roads.
issues.why: The front stabilizer bar links or bushings wear out.
issues.next: Have the front end checked. Sway bar links are inexpensive and usually replaced in pairs.

issues.t: Rattle or clatter on start-up
issues.sym: A loud clatter for a second or two after a cold start, especially after the car sat overnight.
issues.why: The timing chain tensioner or cam phaser oil control valve lets the chain or phasers rattle until oil pressure builds. Hyundai later issued a bulletin changing the timing chain and crankshaft sprockets on these engines. A few owners found metal in the oil and needed a new engine.
issues.next: Have a dealer check it on a cold start and look for the timing chain bulletin. Keep up with oil changes, and get a second opinion if told it is normal and it keeps getting worse.

issues.t: Clicking or clunk when turning the steering wheel
issues.sym: A click, clack or thud from the steering column when turning the wheel, often over bumps.
issues.why: The rubber coupling between the electric power steering motor and the steering column wears out. Hyundai released a more durable coupling.
issues.next: It does not affect steering control, but have the coupling replaced with the updated part.

issues.t: Steering feels stuck or notchy at highway speed
issues.sym: At highway speed the steering seems to stick in place and needs a firm push before it responds, or reacts late to small corrections.
issues.why: Several owners reported this to NHTSA. No cause has been confirmed, and dealers often could not reproduce it; it points to the electric power steering system.
issues.next: If it happens, keep a firm grip and slow down. Write down when it happens and ask the dealer to scan the steering module and road test at highway speed.

issues.t: Harsh, delayed or slipping shifts
issues.sym: Jerky shifts, a pause before the car engages Drive or Reverse, engine speed flaring between gears, or a check engine light for an incorrect gear ratio.
issues.why: Hyundai issued several bulletins for this 6-speed automatic covering harsh or delayed shifts, clutch wear relearning and clutch slipping.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check the transmission software, fluid level and type before replacing fluid or parts. Slipping needs prompt diagnosis.

issues.t: Shifter will not come out of Park
issues.sym: With the engine running and the brake pressed, the shifter sometimes will not move out of Park.
issues.why: Hyundai issued bulletins for this 6-speed shifter on certain cars.
issues.next: Most shifters have a manual release slot to move it out of Park. Have a dealer check the bulletin and the brake light switch.

issues.t: Fogging or water inside headlights and tail lights
issues.sym: Condensation or droplets inside the headlights, tail lights, daytime running lights or fog lights.
issues.why: Moisture builds up inside the lamp housings. Hyundai issued bulletins on how to judge and repair it.
issues.next: Light fog that clears is normal. Pooled water or failing bulbs means the lamp should be repaired or replaced.

issues.t: Passenger airbag may deploy with wrong force (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger airbag status light may show the wrong state for who is sitting in the seat.
issues.why: The occupant detection system in the passenger seat could misjudge an adult, child or child seat on cars built May-November 2012.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 13V-264; the dealer recalibrates the system.

issues.t: Trunk cannot be opened from inside (recall)
issues.sym: The trunk is hard to open or close, or the inside emergency release does not open it.
issues.why: Damage to the trunk latch can stop the inside release from working, so the car does not meet the federal trunk release standard.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 21V-619; the dealer replaces the latch base for free.

issues.t: Check engine light from oxygen or cam sensors
issues.sym: Check engine light, sometimes with rough running, hesitation or poorer fuel economy.
issues.why: Oxygen sensors and camshaft position sensors are frequent failures on these cars, according to owner repair records.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Replace the sensor the code points to and clear the codes; a loose gas cap can also set a light.

issues.t: Cooling fan runs constantly or does not run
issues.sym: The radiator fan keeps running after the car is off, roars all the time, or does not come on so the engine runs hot in traffic.
issues.why: The cooling fan relay or fan control module fails.
issues.next: Watch the temperature gauge. If the fan does not run and the engine heats up in traffic, pull over and have the fan relay and module tested.
